svg.text: K4b MAT STORE + GATE — hung in a slot, washed on the way in, steamed there
Two solid silicone mats (S raw, D dough / ready-to-eat); a 5 kg dancer keeps 25 N; never wound, never stored wet.
mat 280 × 1550 × 2 mm, platinum silicone 70 Shore A, no fabric
slot 55 × 300 × 770, dancer Ø 50 × 300, 5 kg, 650 mm travel
gate: lips, cold rinse, 60 °C detergent, 85 °C rinse, squeegee
steam ≥ 95 °C for 60 s (A0 ≈ 1900 s) · 65 °C air 4 min
A SLOT D (section): out, back through the gate, steamed, dried

text.tspan: parked: almost the whole mat hangs in the slot
the arm draws the hem out; the dancer rises
in use: food on the mat (≤ 1.3 m out)
retraction at 50 mm/s through the gate: washed
steam fills the closed slot: ≥ 95 °C for 60 s

svg.text: After every class-R use (mat S) and daily (mat D). Mat change: 2 min, no tools.
B THE GATE: what a point of the mat meets on its way down (no actuator, lips always closed)
gross soil falls back onto the table
recirculated from a 3 L sump through a strainer
camera C1 sees the back face
C THE MAT: solid silicone, nothing to hide soil
edge bead 4 × 5, root fillet R 2.5, no undercut
edge marks every 50 mm → camera measures the feed
hem: Ø 8 steel rod moulded fully in — no pocket
Strain at 25 N: 0.7 % → no fabric core needed. Life 2–3 years, ≈ €80 per mat.
Mat S: raw meat, fish, breading, Rouladen. Mat D: dough, washed produce, cooked food, assembly.

g.text: 1/6 Parked: the mat hangs as a U round the dancer in its own closed slot; only the hem lies on the table
2/6 The arm takes the hem and draws the mat over the table; the 5 kg dancer rises and keeps 25 N tension
3/6 In use: food on the mat; the capstan nose E feeds and returns it
4/6 Drawn back: both faces pass scraper lips, cold rinse, 60 °C detergent, 85 °C rinse and squeegee
5/6 In the closed slot: steam ≥ 95 °C for 60 s disinfects mat, dancer and walls
6/6 Warm air dries it hanging — the mat is never wound and never stored wet
